newsitem.title: TURKEY: Kurd MP threatens revelations in Turkey scandal.
newsitem.headline: Kurd MP threatens revelations in Turkey scandal.

text.p: A Kurdish MP and warlord at the centre of a row over alleged links between Turkey's powerful security apparatus and far-right gangsters has threatened to reveal more details of the scandal.
Government MP Sedat Bucak said in remarks published on Thursday he would name names in the ruling elite who had ties to late fugitive mobster Abdullah Catli.
The main opposition Motherland Party (ANAP) took to the streets to tap into public distaste at the scandal and gather signatures for a petition aiming to restrict MPs' immunity from prosecution.

"There were a lot of people who knew Catli," the Gozcu newspaper quoted Bucak as saying in an interview. "If I get up and speak -- and I will speak when the time is right -- I don't know what they are going to do," he said.
Kurdish tribal chief Bucak acknowledged a close friendship with Catli, a suspected heroin smuggler wanted for the murder of seven leftist militants in the late 1970s.

"I loved him as one loves a big brother," Bucak said in his first public comments since a fatal crash earlier this month that raised still unanswered questions about possible ties between leading officials and the right-wing underworld.
Bucak was the only survivor from a car carrying Catli, a senior policeman and a former beauty queen that crashed in the town of Susurluk in western Turkey.
Bucak, a member of Tansu Ciller's junior coalition partner True Path Party (DYP), has not been questioned by police.
But six of his bodyguards were quizzed by a prosecutor on Wednesday about allegations in the press that they were involved in the murder in Istanbul of a casino owner earlier this year.
Dozens of people queued up in central Ankara's main street to sign an ANAP petition calling for MPs' wideranging protection from prosecution to be loosened.
"They are taking advantage of us with the immunity we gave them. Sedat Bucak and the Susurluk affair for example. It's a complete disgrace," student Dogan Cakmak said.
The party, which also gathered signatures in downtown Istanbul, plans to hand a petition to parliament.
The scandal forced then interior minister Mehmet Agar to resign amid allegations that he had met the crash victims in a seaside resort a day before the accident.
